text:
[LCYC.2.3.1] Each rule fires only if the other's fact is
absent, and each rule's firing asserts a fact
that makes the other's condition false. The smallest case is two rules:
`x`, whose one pattern is `no Y` and whose RHS is `emit X logical`, and `y`,
whose one pattern is `no X` and whose RHS is `emit Y logical`.

idris.name: lcyc_2_3_1__defeat0
idris.note: The pair from empty working memory: both `no`s unblocked, both eligible.

idris.name: lcyc_2_3_1__defeat_prog
idris.note: The clause's pair, over EXPLICIT facts where the clause writes `emit X logical`. The run is the same -- one firing, then the loser's `no` is blocked for good -- because the winner's justifier (`no Y`) never stops holding, so the TMS would never retract X; but the TMS is not in this engine, so that is argued, not proved.

idris.name: lcyc_2_3_1__defeat_x
idris.note: The clause's `rule x: no Y y -> emit X`.

idris.name: lcyc_2_3_1__defeat_y
idris.note: The clause's `rule y: no X x -> emit Y`.
